Maya K: Heads up — hitting SSL failures with the Python SDK on Windows + Python 3.11 in a venv. Works fine on Linux and older 3.9 boxes.
Maya K: Error shows up when initialising the client and doing a simple request, looks like cert verification fails in the embedded SSL stack.
Maya K: ```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "example.py", line 42, in <module>
    resp = client.text.generate(...)
  File ".../site-packages/requests/sessions.py", line 614, in get
    resp = self.request('GET', url, **kwargs)
requests.exceptions.SSLError: [SSL: CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED] certificate verify failed: unable to get local issuer certificate (_ssl.c:997)
```
Maya K: Repro steps: Windows 11, python 3.11.4 from python.org, venv with `py -3.11 -m venv .venv`, pip install -r requirements (includes our sdk 0.7.0). Using corporate proxy but proxy cert is installed in Windows cert store.
Shiv P: @Maya K good find — do you know which OpenSSL / ssl backend is being used? CPython on windows should prefer Windows cert store but some wheels bundle OpenSSL which can change precedence.
Maya K: I checked `ssl.OPENSSL_VERSION` -> shows OpenSSL 3.0.10 and `sys.version` shows the python.org build. Repro is consistent: 3.9 (same machine) works, 3.11 fails.
Alice L: Quick try: can you install certifi and point SSL_CERT_FILE to certifi.where() as a temporary workaround? e.g. `pip install certifi` then in powershell `setx SSL_CERT_FILE "$(python -c "import certifi; print(certifi.where())")"` and restart shell.
Ben T: Also try programmatic context override in your script to see if the client honors ssl contexts. Example:
```python
import ssl, certifi
ctx = ssl.create_default_context(cafile=certifi.where())
# if SDK exposes client param for ssl_context
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=..., ssl_context=ctx)
# or for requests session fallback
session = requests.Session()
session.verify = certifi.where()
```
Ben T: If that fixes it, it's a precedence/load path bug we can patch in the SDK to prefer certifi when present or accept an explicit SSL context for both sync+async clients.
Maya K: Tried certifi env var — that fixes the request, so this is definitely a cert resolution precedence issue in some Windows/Python combos. Thanks. :relieved:
Maya K: Small repro script I ran:
```python
import requests, ssl, certifi, platform, sys
print(platform.platform(), sys.version)
print('openssl', ssl.OPENSSL_VERSION)
print('certifi', certifi.where())
requests.get('https://example.com')
```
# on 3.11 this raises SSLError, on 3.9 it succeeds
cert-bot: Created INF-3421: "py sdk: windows 3.11 venv cert verification precedence" — https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-3421 :white_check_mark:
Shiv P: Thanks — filing an SDK bug is good. For short-term: we should add docs to the quickstart for Windows users (call out SSL_CERT_FILE / certifi) and publish a small patch to accept `ssl_context` on AsyncClient as well.
Shiv P: @Alice L can you paste the draft text for the quickstart snippet? would be helpful to ship with the patch.
Alice L: Draft snippet: `If you encounter CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED on Windows, install certifi and set SSL_CERT_FILE to certifi.where() or pass an ssl.SSLContext with cafile=certifi.where() to the client.` I'll open a docs PR.
Ben T: I'm going to prototype a tiny change to the HTTP layer to prefer explicit `SSL_CERT_FILE` env, then certifi, then system. Also add param to AsyncClient ctor: `ssl_context: Optional[ssl.SSLContext] = None` — will run through typestubs and mypy checks so typing stays clean.
Shiv P: PR incoming? drop link when ready so QE can smoke test across py3.8-3.12 + Win/Lin.
Ben T: https://github.com/redwood-inference/python-sdk/pull/215 (draft) — adds ssl_context passthrough + certifi precedence, updates type stubs for AsyncClient.
Maya K: Tested a locally built wheel from that branch — confirms fix on my 3.11 venv. No more SSLError. Thanks all! :tada:
Maya K: Will attach logs to INF-3421 and mark repro steps. Leaving this thread open until docs + release cut.
cert-bot: INF-3421 status updated -> triaged (priority: P2)
Ben T: I'll add a small changelog note and cut a patch release after docs PR is merged, planning 0.7.1.
Maya K: Awesome, appreciate the fast turnaround. :thumbsup:
